newsitem.title: USA: NYC sets top yield for retail orders in bond sale.
newsitem.headline: NYC sets top yield for retail orders in bond sale.

text.p: New York City on Friday started its retail order period for an offering of $900 million of bonds, setting the top yield in 2027 at 6.35 percent, Smith Barney said.
The bonds will be offered to institutional investors on April 9, when the prices will be finalized.

For the $600 million sale of new money bonds, Smith Barney, the lead underwriter, said that for serial bonds, the yields ranged from 4.60 percent for the 1999 maturity to 6.25 percent for the 2017 issue.
In addition to the 2027 maturity, the other term bond, which matures in 2017, was priced at a yield of 6.25 percent.

And for the approximately $301.6 million sale, yields for the serial bonds ranged from 4.60 percent in 1997 to 6.20 percent for 2013. The two term issues were priced at 6.25 percent in 2017, and 6.30 percent in 2021.
